report.source_text: During the TEE, the following findings were reported: ejection fraction (EF) of 40–45%; very severe aortic aneurysm (AI); dilated aortic aneurysm measuring 6.9 cm; mild mitral regurgitation (MR); minimal tricuspid regurgitation (TR); mild pulmonary insufficiency (PI); pulmonary artery pressure (PAP) of 50 mm/Hg; severe left ventricle enlargement measuring 136 cm/m2 with mild systolic dysfunction; a large (1.1 cm) semi-mobile mass on the arterial side of the noncoronary cusp (NCC) mostly resembling vegetation; very severe aortic regurgitation (AR), aneurysmal aortic root (annulus, 3.1 cm; sinus of valsalva (SOV), 4.2 cm; effacement of sinotubular junction (STJ)); aneurysmal dilation of the ascending aorta with the proximal portion measuring 6.8 cm and the distal portion measuring 3.9 cm; a visible linear flap of aortic dissection originating about 1.3 cm after the aortic valve (AV); the dissecting flap appearing thickened and infected; and mild circumferential pericardial effusion (5 mm around all cardiac chambers).

clinician.trajectory_summary: A 31-year-old man presented with fever and chills. Brain MRI revealed multiple cortical infarcts indicating embolic phenomena. Transthoracic echocardiography identified a large (7.7 cm) aortic aneurysm. Transesophageal echocardiography showed a dilated aortic aneurysm (6.9 cm), severe aortic regurgitation, a large semi-mobile vegetation on the aortic valve noncoronary cusp, and an aortic dissection with an infected flap. These findings indicated infective endocarditis complicated by aortic aneurysm and dissection. Surgical intervention was performed with replacement of the aortic valve and ascending aorta via Bentall procedure. Post-operatively, the patient was admitted to ICU and continued antibiotic therapy.
